title: MOE Elite Scholarship
deadline_central_display: No single MOE deadline - apply through the participating university's admission application, following the document deadline in the post-admission email
deadline_note: Each participating university sets its own admission window; application timelines differ by school. Students in the African programme start in the spring semester and those from New Southbound countries and South Asia start in the fall semester. After admission, applicants receive an email from the Office of International Affairs with the application deadline for MOE-Elite document submission.
application_cycle: Two intakes a year (New Southbound Policy Countries and South Asian countries in the fall semester; African countries in the spring semester), with Ministry announcements around late October and late April
status_note: The scholarship is listed on participating universities' official sites with no published application deadline, and the Ministry of Education notifies recipient lists around late October (fall semester) and late April (African students).
tuition_coverage_note: Participating universities describe the scholarship as including a tuition waiver; the NT$25,000 per month is the total monthly award from which tuition and credit fees are deducted at some institutions.
benefits: Tuition subsidy (a tuition waiver is included in the award)
100 students per academic year over three academic years, a total of 300 students
Supported by the Ministry of Education with humanities education, observatory visits and career planning, with mentoring by university teachers and industry professionals
eligibility: Lecturer, assistant professor, associate professor or professor at a public or private higher education institution in an eligible country
Must hold an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English
Those who are international applicants from countries on the MOE eligible country list
Must be admitted to a Master's degree programme through the normal admissions process
Wish to pursue a graduate degree in Taiwan and be selected in a screening
requirements: Teaching position must be characterised by temporary or long-term leave during the study period; the work obligation is handled in accordance with the university and country's regulations
Those who hold ROC nationality or enrolled with overseas Chinese student status are excluded
Those enrolled or retained at a university in Taiwan are excluded
Those who have studied at an academic level in Taiwan or in another country are excluded
International exchange students and dual degree students with a collaborative study agreement with a foreign school are excluded
Those who have received stipends or subsidies from this programme for more than three years are excluded
Students receiving other government scholarships or subsidies are excluded
Submit the MOE-Elite form and the Lecturer Certificate by the deadline stated in the email from the Office of International Affairs
Enrolment procedures must be completed every semester, with tuition and fees to be paid each semester
coverage: NT$25,000 per month, of which tuition and credit fees are deducted at some participating universities
Tuition waiver included in the award
application_method: Apply to a participating university selecting a full English-taught PhD programme and submit the MOE-Elite form together with the Lecturer Certificate in English by the stated deadline
Some universities require students to apply online before immigrating to Taiwan and take priority English interviews
application_route: Apply to a participating university choosing a full English-taught programme; after admission, submit the MOE-Elite form and Lecturer Certificate by the deadline stated in the email from the university's Office of International Affairs.
duration: Up to 2 years for a master's programme and up to 3 years for a doctoral programme, subject to annual review; some participating universities run the programme for up to 4 years
description: The Ministry of Education Elite Scholarship is a scholarship programme for international applicants from countries on the MOE eligible country list who wish to pursue a graduate degree in Taiwan, providing a full tuition fee subsidy and a monthly stipend.

not_confirmed: the MOE's own English page for the Elite Scholarship (only the programme summary listing could be located on MOE's English site)
whether the full NT$25,000 reaches the student, which differs by university
verification.notes: Participating universities publish the terms of the MOE Elite Scholarship on their own official .edu.tw domains. National Pingtung University of Science and Technology states the programme 'provides full tuition fee subsidy for outstanding university lecturers from selected New Southbound Policy Countries, South Asian countries, and African countries' and that the Ministry notifies recipient lists around 25 October (fall semester) and 25 April (African students). National Taipei University of Technology states the scholarship 'provides full tuition waiver and monthly stipend for outstanding university lecturers from selected New Southbound, South Asian, and African countries who are admitted to PhD programs at Taipei Tech', that it offers '4 years of full tuition waiver + monthly stipend', that the MOE revised the title for international students to Elite Scholarships Programme for New Southbound Policy Countries and South Asian Countries/Elite Scholarships Programme for African Countries and that applications are 'accepted throughout the academic year, whereas it resumes from 1.3 to 1.31 each year', and that the 1st to 3rd year stipend is around NT$14,000 per month and the 4th year NT$12,000 per month. National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University describes the purpose and states 'Monthly stipends NT$ 25,000 and a tuition waiver for 3 years' and that recipients receive the scholarship on the 10th of each month except January and the start of each semester (September). Because participating universities describe the award differently - NTUT describes NT$25,000 as the total monthly award with tuition deducted, while NYCU describes a separate tuition waiver - the exact cash amount in hand varies by institution and should be confirmed with the specific university. The MOE's own page for this subsidy could not be reached directly; terms were taken from participating universities' official pages, which is why confidence is recorded as medium rather than high.

applicant_utility: This is aimed squarely at university lecturers and professors rather than recent graduates, and you have to hold an up-to-date Lecturer Certificate in English to be considered. You also must enrol in a programme in which every course is taught in English, so a partially English-taught degree will rule you out. The advertised NT$25,000 a month is the headline figure, but be careful: some participating universities describe it as the total monthly award from which tuition and credit fees are deducted, which leaves you with considerably less in hand than NT$25,000, while others describe a separate tuition waiver. Confirm the mechanics with the specific university before you resign from your post at home. You cannot combine it with other Taiwanese government scholarships, and it is annual review rather than automatic renewal - up to two years for a master's and up to three for a doctorate, though some universities run it for four. Applications happen as part of the admissions process to a participating university; after admission you get an email from the Office of International Affairs with a closing date for submitting the MOE-Elite form and your Lecturer Certificate, so watch that closely.

title: MOE Short-term Research Award
discipline: Humanities discipline, social sciences, culture/arts field, or comparative research related to Taiwan
deadline_central_display: Applications must arrive at the host institution by 30 September each year
deadline_note: Applications must arrive at the host institution no later than 30 September for research conducted the following year. The Ministry conducts preliminary reviews and interviews.
application_cycle: Annual; applications to the host institution by 30 September, with preliminary reviews and interviews
status_note: Applications are made annually with a 30 September deadline for research conducted the following year.
benefits: Monthly research allowance of NTD $25,000 for a Ph.D student or NT $40,000 for a postdoctoral fellow
An economy class round-trip airfare for the most direct route between their place of residence and Taiwan
A research stay in Taiwan for between 2 and 6 months
eligibility: The research project must be related to Taiwan
The research topic must be in a humanities discipline, social sciences, culture/arts field, or a related comparative research topic
The applicant must hold a PhD degree or be a PhD student
Applicants must be proficient in Chinese, English and/or other foreign languages
Researchers with established academic positions at foreign universities or institutions may apply as senior researchers
Only one applicant per proposed advisor is accepted
Applicants must be citizens of a country with legal sovereignty - those without a country of jurisdiction or with citizenship of anonymous countries (Palestine) cannot apply
requirements: Applications must arrive at the host institution no later than 30 September for research conducted the following year
Attend preliminary reviews and interviews conducted by the Ministry
coverage: Monthly research allowance of NTD $25,000 for a PhD student or NT $40,000 for a postdoctoral fellow
application_method: Submit an application to the selected host institution, reaching it no later than 30 September
application_route: Secure a host institution in Taiwan, then submit the application so it reaches the host institution by 30 September.
duration: Between 2 and 6 months of research in Taiwan
description: The Ministry of Education Short-term Research Award supports foreign academics to conduct research in Taiwan in the humanities or social sciences, providing a monthly research allowance and round-trip airfare.

not_confirmed: selection criteria beyond the preliminary review and interview
verification.notes: Monthly research allowance for both PhD student and postdoctoral fellow, the economy class round-trip airfare, the 2 to 6 month research period, the 30 September host institution deadline, the research field requirements and both eligibility and exclusion lists were all read directly from the Ministry of Education Taiwan official scholarship page, which quotes from the Regulations Governing the Ministry of Education's Awards and Subsidies for Foreigners Undertaking Short-term Study in Taiwan.

applicant_utility: This is a short research stay rather than a degree, so it suits a researcher who wants between two and six months of Taiwan fieldwork in the humanities or social sciences. The funding is solidly distinguished by career stage: PhD students receive NT$25,000 a month and postdoctoral fellows NT$40,000 a month, and everyone gets economy-class round-trip airfare for the most direct route. The application deadline is the one to plan around - it must reach the host institution by 30 September for research conducted the following year, so contact your prospective host well before July. Your project must be genuinely Taiwan-related and sit in the humanities, social sciences, culture or arts, or a related comparative field. Only one applicant per proposed advisor is accepted, so if you are approaching a well-known Taiwan scholar it pays to write early. Note that the rules exclude applicants without a country of jurisdiction and those holding citizenship of countries such as Palestine, which is a hard eligibility bar.
